newsitem.title: JAPAN: NYK Fed chief says supports Rubin on strong dollar.
newsitem.headline: NYK Fed chief says supports Rubin on strong dollar.

text.p: William McDonough, president of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, told reporters on Tuesday that he shares U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin's stance on a strong dollar.

Asked about recent currency market movements, McDonough said although the only official U.S. spokesman on currencies was Rubin, he believed in Rubin's stance that a strong dollar was in U.S. interests.
"(Rubin) continues to reiterate something I firmly believe in, that a strong dollar is in the U.S.'s interests," he said.
McDonough declined to comment on the impact of recent currency movements on the U.S. economy.

Asked about the outlook for the economies of both Japan and the United States, he said Japanese authorities seemed to have a high degree of confidence that growth in the current fiscal year would continue to be quite strong.
He said he hoped growth in the United States would continue and added that he believed the same would happen in Japan in the next fiscal year.
McDonough said data showing a rise in hourly wages in the United States was not important in itself and added that he would have to see what its inflationary impact would be.
